title: Custom providers — round 2, your notes applied

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → Add provider
steps.headline: Add provider is now a card like OpenRouter's, and Cancel appears only once there is something to add.
steps.changed: Empty: a title, one grey line, the search box and ✕. Picked: "Inception (api.inceptionlabs.ai)", name "Inception API Key", then Cancel and Add provider.
steps.notice: It looks like the other cards and only shows what you can do next.

steps.headline: A picked service's models are a fold of cards, each with its context size, price and tool use.
steps.changed: Under the search box, "Models 4" opens one card per model: name, then chips for context (1M, 260K…), price in and out per million, and "No tools" where a model can't use them.
steps.notice: You see what you are getting — Mercury 3's 1M context and $0.10 / $0.35 price — before you paste a key.
steps.risk: These numbers come from the public catalog; your own account may differ slightly.

steps.path: Add provider → paste a key → Add provider
steps.headline: Saved providers are the same card too: name with its address in brackets, buttons and switch at the top right.
steps.changed: The lighter hand-made row is gone. "Inception API Key (api.inceptionlabs.ai)" sits on the top line with Edit, Test, Remove and the on/off switch at the right; a rejected key keeps its red notice inside the card.
steps.notice: Every card on Cloud providers now has one shape, whether it is OpenRouter, ChatGPT or a key you added.

steps.path: Chat → model menu → search for a model that isn't listed
steps.headline: "No models match" is now a full sentence at normal size, with a small centred button under it.
steps.changed: It names your search and says new models can take a day to appear; "Check for new models" is a small button centred below. The footer now reads "Manage models and providers…".
steps.notice: The sentence explains why the model is missing before offering the fix.

steps.headline: Should the design guide gain two rules so forms and menus can't drift from the rest of the page again?
steps.today: The guide covers cards, buttons and notices, but says nothing about how a form that adds an item to a list should look, or that search menus must use the app's one dropdown.
steps.problem: Round 1 drew Add provider as a plain box with its own menu shape, and nothing in the guide said that was wrong — the gap you called out.
steps.proposal: Two rules. Yes adds both to the guide's Cards and Lists sections; No leaves the guide as it is.

options.label: Add both rules
options.summary: "A form that adds an item to a list of cards is drawn as one of those cards — title, grey line, ✕ at the top right, its buttons at the bottom right once there is something to add." and "Every dropdown or search menu is the shared one: same corner, row size and highlighted choice."
pros: The next form or menu starts from the right shape.
Reviews can point to a written rule.
cons: Two more rules to keep current.

options.label: Only the form rule
cons: A one-off menu could still slip through.
